answer: Tie every account to an anchor: a small time-locked stake that is forfeited if two of its attestations ever trace back to the same operator, so cloning costs real money. Weave each account's history into a thread of endorsements from strangers on different ridges of the network: a thread that loops back to the same few names frays and loses weight, while one that spans distant ridges strengthens. Finally, make the ridge itself move: reputation earned on one ridge only counts on another after fresh work there, so a Sybil farm cannot copy one good record across many identities.
